scope_limit: MAIN_RIV groups and model mainstem roles do not establish a uniform name for every included reach, tributary or lake passage. Source observations support only the stated representative identity or hold.
publication_boundary: Own factual observations, attribution and official public URLs only; source originals, images, complete coordinates and private evidence remain omitted.

correspondence.component_scope: Ramsdale–Coyote northern canyon approach
correspondence.finding: The opening is in the Ramsdale Canyon setting east of the low northern hills, turns northwest and west through the canyon notch near Canyon Tank, crosses the highway corridor and continues southwest through the Coyote Canyon setting. The topographic corridor is legible. Canyon labels are not promoted to an established stream name.
correspondence.correspondence: Headward landform corridor read; no whole-system hydronym established

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern Malpais margin and Nogal Creek approach
correspondence.finding: The selected course runs south along the eastern edge of the northern lava field, in the White Oaks Draw setting, toward the mapped westward Nogal Creek approach north and west of Carrizozo. Nogal Creek reaches the lava margin. Neither its label nor the adjoining valley establishes a continuous selected southward channel beyond this contact.
correspondence.correspondence: Lava-margin terrain and lateral named-creek approach read; through-going axial stream unresolved

correspondence.component_scope: Carrizozo lava-neck and southwestern margin
correspondence.finding: The route continues southwest along the Carrizozo Malpais terrain, crosses the narrow lava corridor, and follows its western/southwestern margin opposite the Phillips Hills. Cottonwood Creek and other eastern drainage terminate at or approach the other side of the lava. The detailed original maps show the lava relief and local water features, but not one continuous surface channel corresponding to this full axial transfer. The field-study observation F2 is relevant; it does not establish a present connector.
correspondence.correspondence: Entire selected lava corridor mapped; current watercourse continuity not established

correspondence.component_scope: Western lava-margin transfer to Salt Creek
correspondence.finding: The selected route turns west through the low plain from the lava margin toward Salt Creek downstream of the Salt Springs reach. A short isolated water feature occurs near the lava edge, and Salt Creek is clearly drawn to the west. The intervening selected watercourse and its junction are not established merely by the shared low plain. The separately mapped Malpais Spring channel farther southeast is not substituted for this selected transfer.
correspondence.correspondence: Selected transfer and Salt Creek receiving corridor read; connector not established

correspondence.component_scope: Mapped Salt Creek middle and lower channel
correspondence.finding: The selected route joins the directly drawn Salt Creek corridor, follows it southwest beside the San Andres piedmont, rounds the large bend, and runs southeast and south past the range-road crossings toward the playa complex. Mapped lateral washes and spring/wetland features remain distinct. Continuous river correspondence is supported here despite generalized model bends.
correspondence.correspondence: Positive ordinary corridor-scale channel correspondence

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Salt Creek and Big Salt Lake playa margin
correspondence.finding: The lower selected portion reaches the Salt Creek / Big Salt Lake playa setting. The mapped Salt Creek channel turns into the playa complex while the selection continues along its western/southern side. This supplies a bounded receiving-playa setting, not a demonstrated outlet through the dune-fringed terrain to the south. See field-study observation F1 and Figure 1.
correspondence.correspondence: Lower named-channel and adjacent receiving-playa setting read; onward continuation unresolved

correspondence.component_scope: Southward dune-fringed transfer and western basin-floor bend
correspondence.finding: The selection extends south past the playa complex, then bends west across the basin floor before turning south toward Alkali Flat. Original cartography depicts dune relief, flats and roads, without a continuous selected waterway. F1 is affirmative field evidence of obstruction between these playa and Alkali Flat settings. It is not interpreted as proving that every conceivable flood route is impossible; it does prevent treating the selected connection as established.
correspondence.correspondence: Terrain covered; actual selected drainage connector unestablished

correspondence.component_scope: Alkali Flat and northern Lake Lucero approach
correspondence.finding: The selected line crosses the Alkali Flat / White Sands National Park floor and reaches the northern Lake Lucero playa margin. This long flat crossing is not drawn as a through-going stream. The mapped Andrecito Creek approach from the west reaches the northern lake area separately; it does not supply the missing northern connector.
correspondence.correspondence: Closed-basin floor and lakeward approach mapped; continuous channel unestablished

correspondence.component_scope: Lake Lucero terminal
correspondence.finding: The final selected parts lie within the mapped Lake Lucero playa/lake complex and finish in that terminal setting. The lake identity and closed-basin surroundings are supported. No ocean outlet is claimed, and this lake setting does not establish the upstream cross-flat connection.
correspondence.correspondence: Actual terminal waterbody setting established

primary_field_study_observations.location: Printed page 145, right column, first full paragraph; Figure 1, printed page 144
primary_field_study_observations.observation: The authors identify Holocene dunes as blocking the southward path from the Salt Creek–Big/Little Salt Lake playa complex to Alkali Flat. Their Figure 1 locates the playas, dunes, Salt Creek and Alkali Flat. This is evidence of a geomorphic obstruction, not just an absent river name.

primary_field_study_observations.location: Printed page 145, right column, final paragraph
primary_field_study_observations.observation: The field study says the Carrizozo lava flow buried an earlier axial alluvial channel and stopped before Salt Creek valley. That historical channel is not evidence of an uninterrupted current surface stream along the selected lava corridor.

primary_field_study_observations.location: Printed page 145, right column, Salt Creek paragraph
primary_field_study_observations.observation: The authors distinguish perennial Salt Creek beginning at Salt Springs from commonly ephemeral flow farther downstream to Big Salt Lake. Seasonal or dry reaches are therefore not rejected merely for lacking perennial water.

correspondence.component_scope: Headward opening and northern bend
correspondence.finding: The opening south of Iguaçu follows the mapped Cangati corridor north through the Iguaçu/Fazenda São Luís setting, then bends east through the São Salvador/Monte Vilar and Juá setting toward Piedade and Targinos. Canindé shows the connected stream path, local Campos and Cangati labels, the Serra Pintada/Talhada setting and separate Boqueirão, Tanques, Logradouro and Canjari tributaries. These source channels establish the selected opening rather than basin membership alone; precise hydronym transition points remain unassigned.
correspondence.correspondence: Entire selected opening and its eastward transfer read

correspondence.component_scope: Eastward Cangati approach
correspondence.finding: The mapped Cangati runs east through Targinos, Mulungu/Quintiliano and Lajes, bends through Barbada and continues past Várzea Queimada and Santa Fé. Canindé and Itapiúna overlap this route. The south-arriving Guaribas, Barbada/Boa Fortuna and Caçadas drainage and northern small tributaries are mapped as lateral approaches rather than replacements for the selected western route.
correspondence.correspondence: Continuous upper approach across the adjoining municipal sheets read

correspondence.component_scope: Cangati–Choró confluence south of Caio Prado
correspondence.finding: The Cangati makes its southern bend and turns east past the Canafístula/Fazenda Volta setting to the mapped junction at Fazenda Boa Sorte. The separately drawn Choró arrives from the south and continues north past Caio Prado. The selection follows the west-arriving Cangati and then the northward Choró; it does not include the southern Choró headwaters.
correspondence.correspondence: Actual selected tributary-to-receiving-river connector read

correspondence.component_scope: Choró through Itans and the Castro/Pesqueiro junctions
correspondence.finding: The mapped receiving channel passes Bico da Arara, Barra Nova, Curtume and Itans, then Choró dos Batista, Monte Alegre/Mondubim and Choró Junco. Rio Castro joins from the west near the Itapiúna-side bend. The route continues northeast toward the Pesqueiro junction near Lagoinha, then Plácido Martins. The Pesqueiro/Pedra Branca approach is distinct from the selected southwestern Choró.
correspondence.correspondence: Selected northeastward river and major side connections read

correspondence.component_scope: Aracoiaba-area middle corridor to Chorozinho
correspondence.finding: The selected route follows the Choró north from Plácido Martins through Vargem Queimada and Várzea da Abelha, then northeast by Ideal and Vazantes/Caxingó. Rio Aracoiaba and the Jaguarão/Pedra Aguda approaches remain lateral. The selected river continues by Criançó, Vargem Grande, Lagoa do Barro and Vila Rosa into Chorozinho. Side Lagoa Nova/Serrote and Aruá streams do not replace this continuous mapped corridor.
correspondence.correspondence: Middle northward/eastward bends and all material junctions read

correspondence.component_scope: Chorozinho approach and Pacajus reservoir passage
correspondence.finding: The mapped Choró continues northeast from Chorozinho and Choró Tapera/Martins through the long southwestern reservoir arm. IBGE Cascavel depicts the water-body expansion and the selected passage toward the eastern narrowing by Choró São Paulo/Jatobá. The Lagamar arm arrives from the west and Arecó from the north toward Pacajus town; neither is the selected main approach. IPECE prints Açude Pacajus at the corresponding water-body setting. COGERH independently identifies Pacajus as impounding Rio Choro. The eastward downstream Choró is separately drawn from the Canal da Integração.
correspondence.correspondence: Actual inflow, selected reservoir arm, narrowing/outlet and first downstream river read

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Choró and actual Atlantic terminal
correspondence.finding: The lower river continues east past Choró Jatobá, Passagem Franca/Mutamba and Umari to the CE-138/CE-040 crossing setting, then turns north between Cascavel and Beberibe past Choró das Pedrinhas and Jacarecoara. The selected ending is the directly mapped coastal Choró outlet beside Barra Nova, with the Atlantic receiving water shown on IBGE. The separate Águas Belas/Caponga-side coastal drainage and eastern Córrego Grande are not substituted for this terminal.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete lower eastward/northward corridor and actual selected coastal outlet read

correspondence.component_scope: Headward opening east of Immokalee, westward loop and southern turn
correspondence.finding: The opening lies by the Immokalee Exchange/County Road 846 corridor, east of the Collier–Hendry boundary. The selected line loops north and west, crosses that boundary, continues southwest past the Thomas Farm Road setting toward State Road 29, then turns southeast through the wetland mosaic toward Wainwright Road and Shoults Grade. USGSTopo depicts marshes, wooded swamps, small ponds and roads throughout, but no continuous mapped river or canal corresponding to this selected opening and long loop. The nearby Summerland Swamp label is not extended to the opening or adopted as a river name. This is unresolved selected waterway correspondence, not just an unnamed but established channel.
correspondence.correspondence: Material selected through-connection remains unestablished; original terrain setting was read.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern Big Cypress approach, first I-75 crossing and eastward wetland reach
correspondence.finding: The selected southward continuation enters northern Big Cypress National Preserve west of the Kissimmee Billy Strand label, crosses the Everglades Parkway/I-75 corridor, and turns east through the marsh/wooded-swamp setting south of the road toward the Florida National Scenic Trail North and Bamboo Strand vicinity. The map clearly distinguishes the West Feeder and North Feeder canals farther north, but neither substitutes for the selected western approach. No mapped through-watercourse establishes the entire southward approach, the selected highway transfer, or the subsequent eastward wetland route. NPS maps and water-resources prose establish a sheet-flow landscape with drainage boundaries and strands, not this particular connector.
correspondence.correspondence: Material selected through-connection remains unestablished; original terrain setting was read.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern Big Cypress, L-28/West Feeder crossings and northeast transfer into Miami Canal
correspondence.finding: The selected route continues east south of I-75, crosses the western boundary/canal setting near the Miccosukee Reservation, turns northeast across I-75, and crosses the broad wetland area toward Miami Canal. USGSTopo independently depicts Interceptor Canal north of the highway, the West Feeder Canal/L-28 setting, a separate north–south canal and the diagonal Miami Canal. It does not show a connected channel or a specific generalized through-flow corridor along the selected east-then-northeast transfer between these mapped features. Mere intersection of the selected model line with mapped canals and membership in the wetland area are not accepted as evidence of junctions. The NPS Hydrology sheet distinguishes Mullet Slough, the drainage boundary, levees and Conservation Area 3A; it still does not establish the selected transfer.
correspondence.correspondence: Material selected through-connection remains unestablished; original terrain setting was read.

correspondence.component_scope: Miami Canal southeastward through the Everglades and I-75 corridor
correspondence.finding: From the selected northeastern turn, the source directly shows the diagonal Miami Canal continuing southeast through the Everglades, crossing I-75 and continuing through the South New River Canal junction and the intersecting canal network. The separate North New River Canal is shown farther east and is not treated as the selected main route. This named-canal corridor corresponds at ordinary generalized scale. Its mapped existence does not establish the preceding wetland entry.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Miami Canal, urban transition and Okeechobee Road corridor
correspondence.finding: The selected southeastward continuation follows the mapped Miami Canal across the Snake Creek Canal setting and the western urban-boundary canal network, then along Okeechobee Road toward Hialeah Gardens, Hialeah and Miami Springs. The source labels the urban reach Miami Canal Number C-6. Nearby lakes, quarry waters, lateral canals and the parallel road are kept separate; no uniform natural-river name is inferred for the canal.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Airport-side canal–river links, Miami River and actual Biscayne Bay terminal setting
correspondence.finding: The map continues C-6 past Miami Springs and the airport/Palmer Lake setting into the North Fork Miami River corridor. It depicts the Tamiami Canal Number C-4 connection, the separate South Fork Miami River, the downstream Miami River and lateral Wagner Creek, then the river opening between downtown Miami and Brickell Point into Biscayne Bay. The entire selected final corridor and actual estuarine terminal setting were read. The retained rendered endpoint is generalized relative to the mapped shoreline; no exact mouth-point or bank agreement is required or claimed.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: FID8818-opening-and-southern-course
correspondence.finding: The selected opening and most of its long initial northward course lie on the continental ice west of Vildtland and west of the Marie Sophie Gletscher/Inuiteq Sø region. The map depicts ice here, not a named river or a lake at the selected opening. Near the northern end of this interval the orientation reaches the southern exposed-rock/ice-margin belt.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.
correspondence.name_scope: Inland Ice, Vildtland, Marie Sophie Gletscher and Inuiteq Sø are contextual feature labels only; none is adopted as this river-group name.

correspondence.component_scope: FID8818-central-bends-and-ice-free-belt

The map allows the central terrain and neighboring valley/lake system to be read on both sides of the selected orientation. It does not depict the selected south-to-north modeled passage as one continuous named river. Continuing north, the selected orientation enters the southern and interior Hans Tavsen Iskappe setting.

No selected lake traversal, lake outlet direction, named-river confluence, or hydraulic transfer from continental ice across the rock belt into Hans Tavsen Iskappe is established merely by the model line. No reservoir is identified on the selected course.

correspondence.component_scope: FID8818-long-westward-ice-cap-course
correspondence.finding: The long westward course and its small northwestward steps are in the Hans Tavsen Iskappe ice/nunatak setting. Toward the west the route approaches the narrow glacier corridor behind the eastern inner arm of Adolf Jensen Fjord. The original does not label this run as a river; the ice-cap name labels the ice body.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.
correspondence.name_scope: Hans Tavsen Iskappe is an ice-cap name, not a representative hydronym for the entire selected object.
correspondence.links: Nearby Odinfjord, Ymer Gletscher and Harebugt belong to the separate eastern side of this mapped region and are not the selected terminal.

correspondence.component_scope: FID8818-final-northwest-turn-and-terminal
correspondence.finding: The final turn reaches the glaciated inner eastern-arm setting of Adolf Jensen Fjord. The original shows the neighboring fjord water, glacier front and ice-filled inward corridor, so the terminal setting can be distinguished from a river mouth at the open coast. This dated generalized map is not used to assert exact present glacier-front or mouth-point agreement.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.
correspondence.terminal_scope: Retained core metadata classifies the terminal as sea. The directly read source supports an inner-fjord/glacier-front setting, not a separately named fluvial mouth or an open-coast river. Adolf Jensen Fjord remains the receiving fjord/place context only.
